title: Working with Remotes: Git Meets GitHub
learning_objectives: Understand the difference between Git (local) and GitHub (remote)
Create a GitHub repository for CatchBook
Connect local repository to GitHub remote with git remote add
Push commits to GitHub with git push
Pull changes from remote with git pull
Understand authentication (SSH keys vs HTTPS tokens)
outline: Git vs GitHub: Local tool vs cloud platform
Why use a remote? Backup, collaboration, deployment
Creating a GitHub account and repository
SSH keys vs HTTPS: Setting up authentication
Connecting local repo to remote: git remote add origin
Pushing code: git push -u origin main (or master)
Cloning repositories: git clone for fresh starts
Fetching vs pulling: git fetch and git pull differences
Hands-on exercise: Push CatchBook repo to GitHub

catchbook_context.feature: CatchBook cloud backup and version history
catchbook_context.deliverable: CatchBook repository on GitHub with initial commits pushed

criteria: Local repository connected to GitHub remote
Can view commit history on GitHub web interface
Understands when to use git push vs git pull

resources.title: Git and GitHub for Beginners - Crash Course

professor_constraints: Help troubleshoot authentication issues (common beginner blocker)
Show both SSH and HTTPS setup, recommend SSH for long-term use
Demonstrate the GitHub web interface to show commits appear there
Address 'what if I make a mistake and push?' question
Use git push -u origin main for first push, explain upstream tracking
Show git remote -v to verify remote connection
Include checkpoint after push/pull explanation (common confusion)
Emphasize: GitHub is backup + collaboration, not just storage
